QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_8

question.text: Which of the following is categorised under 'Investor-level risks' rather than 'Fund-level (governance) risks' in Chapter 7 of the workbook?

answer.text: Lack of transparency and unethical practices in fund governance.
Sub-optimal structuring of investment contracts with investee companies by the manager.
Risk of adverse selection of the fund manager at the time of PPM subscription.
Macroeconomic changes such as currency depreciation affecting foreign LP repatriation.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.1.1, investor-level risks include: Risk of Adverse Selection (choosing the right fund manager), Illiquidity and Uncertainty, Fund Monitoring difficulty, Cash Management for capital calls, Underlying Investment Risks and Debt Financing Risks. Governance/Fiduciary risks, fund management (sub-optimal contracting) and macroeconomic risks (A, B, D) are categorised as Fund-level risks per Section 7.1.2. The Trap: A, B and D are all listed explicitly under Section 7.1.2 Fund-level risks. Adverse selection at the PPM-evaluation stage is uniquely an investor-side risk because the LP has to pick among managers before any fund exists. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A covers the investor-side taxonomy from a distributor pitch. XIX-C tests all three categories combined for all-Cat managers. XV (Research Analyst) touches adverse selection for alternative-assets research recommendations. Manager's Pro-Tip: In your PPM, list adverse-selection risk in the investor-risk section and list governance/fiduciary risks separately — this mirrors SEBI Annexure-1 disclosure template and reduces the chance of SEBI returning the PPM for deficiency.
